clue.text: Beast of a shock about a month back

indicators.note: the word for a shock is placed around the month, so it sits about it

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

indicators.note: back says the abbreviated month is to be read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Aug is the short form of August

explanation.surface: Someone describes a creature that gave them a fright about a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AUG into GUA, and 'about' puts JAR around it: J-GUA-AR.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a big spotted cat of the Americas, a wild animal.

clue.text: Cleric who takes tea on the prairie

parts.note: cha is an old slang word for tea
a prairie is an open grassy plain

explanation.surface: A clergyman out West stops for a cuppa on the open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to a regiment, college or hospital.

clue.text: What alpinists do, presumably, when out on a spree

explanation.surface: Mountaineers out on a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers literally reach lofty points, while the idiom means to enjoy the best nightlife on a spree.

clue.text: Go-ahead fashions at Royal Ascot

parts.note: go-ahead reads as go-a-head: tall formal headwear that goes on the head at the smart racecourse

explanation.surface: Trendy, progressive styles seen at a grand English race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go-ahead' looks like 'progressive' but means things that go on a head. Royal Ascot is a fashionable English horse-race meeting where morning dress is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall silk hats are the traditional headwear of the Royal Enclosure at the races.

clue.text: Short time taken in a milk bar?

explanation.surface: A quick visit to a café selling milkshakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a moment or two, and literally it is two milk drinks ordered at a counter.

clue.text: Suffering of the French in a viva voce test

indicators.note: in puts the French word inside the word for a spoken examination

parts.note: a viva voce is a spoken exam, an oral
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Someone describes the agony of a spoken French exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DE inside ORAL: OR-DE-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, trying experience to be endured.

clue.text: He an artist, she a top Olympian

parts.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A pairing contrasted: a man who paints and a woman at the top of Olympus.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian here means a god on Mount Olympus, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods on Mount Olympus, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Clean Oliver's city

explanation.surface: Tidying up a man's home town.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash oneself or someone in a tub, and the Somerset spa city that gave its name to the Bath Oliver biscuit.

clue.text: Nigerian showing sash back to front

indicators.note: back to front tells us to read the word for a sash in reverse

parts.note: an obi is a broad Japanese sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: A West African man wearing his sash the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibo, or Igbo, are a people of south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: Attractive bird offering one a hair-do?

explanation.surface: A pretty girl offers to style someone's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is 'curl you', said as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a handsome wading bird with a long curved bill; the phrase heard as 'curl you' offers a hairstyling.

clue.text: Preacher's viewpoint on how to mash a potato

explanation.surface: A sermon on the best way to mash potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as 'pulp it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised stand from which a minister preaches, and an instruction to crush the spud to a soft mass.

clue.text: Post for young doctor who feels at home in hospital

definitions.text: who feels at home in hospital

explanation.surface: A junior medic who is comfortable on the wards.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as 'house man', someone at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital doctor in training holds a resident post; read literally, a man at home in the house.

clue.text: Floral embellishment for the knick-knack factory?

explanation.surface: Flowers decorating a works that makes trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: In the second reading 'plant' is a factory and ornaments are knick-knacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative garden flower, and literally a works turning out trinkets.

clue.text: Drink with a bite

explanation.surface: A beverage with a sharp kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, and a small sharp pinch with the teeth.

clue.text: Daredevil performer fair in appearance

parts.note: blond means fair-haired

explanation.surface: A thrill-seeking entertainer who looks fair-haired.
explanation.walkthrough: Blondin was the French tightrope walker who crossed Niagara Falls on a rope in 1859.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous acrobat was a tightrope daredevil who performed stunts over the Niagara gorge.

clue.text: Half-league measure of yarn

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the six letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A distance unit for thread equal to half a league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'league' is a distance unit, but here only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is an old unit of length for yarn, varying with the material.

clue.text: Headgear suitable for the rabble?

parts.note: headwear for the crowd: the common crowd is the mob, and hats are caps

explanation.surface: Asking which hats would suit the common crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A mobcap is a frilly cotton indoor bonnet worn by women in the 18th and 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: These soft frilled bonnets were women's indoor hats, read here as caps for the mob.

clue.text: Weapon for a sullen oarsman

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered or sulky
the bow is the rower nearest the front of the boat

explanation.surface: A grumpy rower carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow fixed on a stock that shoots bolts.

clue.text: Break down in an examination

parts.note: the surface suggests a student collapsing during an exam; the meaning is to split something into its parts while examining it

explanation.surface: A student collapses during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break down' suggests a collapse but means separating into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something in detail by separating it into its elements.

clue.text: Didn't improve matters by producing more inferior goods

explanation.surface: A factory's shoddy output only aggravated the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' joins the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means aggravated a situation; literally, manufactured items of lower quality.

clue.text: Number one by one

parts.note: the figure one written beside another figure one makes a two-digit number

explanation.surface: Counting off individually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one by one' looks like 'singly' but means the digit 1 written beside another 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is the cardinal number that comes after ten.

clue.text: Faster way to fire

indicators.note: way here means a fashion or manner, signalling the letters of the previous word are arranged another way

explanation.surface: A quicker method of shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' tells us to rearrange FASTER; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Lone trip involving crime-fighting co-operative

indicators.note: involving here means entangling or mixing up the letters of the solitary journey

explanation.surface: A solitary journey with an international police body.
explanation.definitionFit: The international criminal police organisation coordinates crime-fighting between national forces.

clue.text: Common spy on Noah's initial craft

indicators.note: initial picks the opening letter of the patriarch's name

parts.note: the ark was Noah's vessel, a craft

explanation.surface: A lowly informer snooping aboard the biblical boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' means slang: nark is British slang for a police informer. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a police informer or stool pigeon, a low spy.

clue.text: Take in with a seagoing rating's eye

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating; the 's adds an S
orb is a poetic word for an eye

explanation.surface: A sailor's watchful gaze takes everything in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak up or take in fully, as a sponge does liquid or the mind does facts.

clue.text: Old city toff clearly has no time to waste

parts.note: Ur was the ancient city of Mesopotamia
a gent, a gentleman, is a toff

explanation.surface: A gentleman from an ancient city is plainly in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearly' links wordplay to definition; the definition describes a matter that brooks no delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter allows no delay, requiring immediate attention.

clue.text: Girl socially acceptable in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the upper-class letter within the abbreviation for the south-east

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east, SE
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in British usage

explanation.surface: A young woman who is well received among posh society near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; U (upper-class) is a British term from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Fish forecast

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A prediction about the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forecast' splits into FORE, the fodder, and 'cast', the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater carp-family fish often kept golden in ponds.
